name: Robert Thompson
chief_complaint: Routine diabetes check-up - feeling more tired lately
opening_statement: I'm here for my diabetes check. I've been feeling more tired than usual over the past few months, and I've noticed I'm getting up to urinate more often at night. My home blood sugar readings have been a bit higher lately.
emotional_baseline: Concerned but cooperative, motivated to improve control

socrates.character: Nocturia 3-4 times per night (increased from baseline of 1-2 times)

rag_citation.source: eTG Endocrine 3.3.1: Type 2 Diabetes - Hyperglycemia Symptoms
rag_citation.quote: Classic hyperglycemia symptoms include polyuria, polydipsia, and fatigue - indicate suboptimal glycemic control

socrates.character: Constant tiredness, reduced energy for usual activities

rag_citation.quote: Chronic fatigue in T2DM may indicate hyperglycemia, anemia (diabetic nephropathy), or hypothyroidism (common comorbidity)
Polydipsia reflects osmotic diuresis from hyperglycemia - resolves with improved glycemic control

rag_citation.source: eTG Endocrine 3.3.2: Type 2 Diabetes Management Targets
rag_citation.quote: HbA1c target for most adults with T2DM is ≤7% (53 mmol/mol) - individualize based on age, comorbidities, hypoglycemia risk

past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed 6 years ago, initially diet-controlled)
Hypertension (10 years, well-controlled on ACE inhibitor)
Obesity (BMI 32 kg/m² - chronic, multiple weight loss attempts)
medications: Perindopril 8mg daily (ACE inhibitor for hypertension + renal protection)
Atorvastatin 40mg nocte (statin for cardiovascular risk reduction)
Aspirin 100mg daily (antiplatelet - secondary prevention in diabetes)
family_history: Father died aged 62 from myocardial infarction (had type 2 diabetes). Mother alive, has hypertension and type 2 diabetes (age 82).

social_history.smoking: Ex-smoker - quit 8 years ago (coinciding with diabetes diagnosis), 20 pack-year history
social_history.alcohol: Moderate - 10-14 standard drinks per week (beer, wine with meals)
social_history.occupation: Truck driver (long-haul, sedentary work, irregular meal times)
social_history.exercise: Minimal - sedentary occupation, no regular exercise routine
social_history.diet: Poor - irregular meals due to work, high carbohydrate intake (sandwiches, pies, soft drinks), limited vegetables
social_history.living_situation: Married, 2 adult children, lives with wife

vitals.bp: 132/82 mmHg (acceptable on treatment - target <140/90 for diabetes)

examination_findings.cardiovascular: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, peripheral pulses palpable bilaterally, no peripheral edema
examination_findings.respiratory: Clear breath sounds bilaterally, no dyspnea at rest
examination_findings.abdomen: Obese, soft, non-tender, no organomegaly palpable
examination_findings.feet: Diabetic foot examination: intact skin, no ulcers, monofilament test normal (protective sensation intact), pedal pulses present bilaterally, no calluses
examination_findings.eyes: Visual acuity 6/6 both eyes (corrected), fundoscopy deferred - refer for retinal screening (due)
examination_findings.neurological: Cranial nerves intact, reflexes present, no peripheral neuropathy on monofilament testing

investigations.hba1c: 8.2% (66 mmol/mol) - ABOVE TARGET (previous 3 months ago: 7.8%, 6 months ago: 7.4%) - WORSENING TREND
investigations.lipids: Total cholesterol 4.8 mmol/L, LDL 2.6 mmol/L, HDL 1.0 mmol/L, Triglycerides 2.4 mmol/L (on statin)
investigations.renal_function: eGFR 72 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD Stage 2 - mild reduction), Creatinine 95 μmol/L
investigations.acr: Albumin:creatinine ratio 4.2 mg/mmol (microalbuminuria - early diabetic nephropathy, requires ACE inhibitor)
investigations.fbc: Hemoglobin 138 g/L (normal), WCC 7.2 x10⁹/L, Platelets 245 x10⁹/L
investigations.retinal_screening: DUE (last screening 18 months ago - overdue, should be annual)
investigations.foot_risk: Low risk (protective sensation intact, pulses present, no deformity)

expected_diagnosis: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with suboptimal glycemic control (HbA1c 8.2%, worsening trend) - requires therapy escalation
expected_management: IMMEDIATE MANAGEMENT:
1. Diabetes Annual Cycle of Care (MBS Item 721 - $67.50) - structured review:
- HbA1c (done - 8.2%, above target)
- Lipids (done - acceptable on statin)
- ACR (done - microalbuminuria detected)
- eGFR (done - CKD Stage 2)
- Retinal screening referral (overdue - due now)
- Diabetic foot examination (done - low risk)
PHARMACOTHERAPY ESCALATION (PBS CRITERIA MET):
2. Add SGLT2 inhibitor: Empagliflozin 10mg daily (PBS restriction: HbA1c >7% on metformin monotherapy ✓)
- Cardiovascular benefits (EMPA-REG trial: 38% reduction in CV death)
- Renal protection (slows eGFR decline, reduces albuminuria)
- Weight loss benefit (average 2-3kg)
- Monitor for genital thrush, euglycemic DKA (rare)
3. Continue metformin 1000mg BD (first-line therapy, continue unless contraindicated)
4. Continue perindopril 8mg daily (ACE inhibitor - ESSENTIAL for microalbuminuria)
5. Continue atorvastatin 40mg nocte (lipid targets acceptable)
NON-PHARMACOLOGICAL MANAGEMENT:
6. Lifestyle modification counseling:
- Diet: Refer to Accredited Practicing Dietitian (MBS Item 10954 - Chronic Disease Management Plan)
- Exercise: Prescribe 150 minutes/week moderate-intensity activity (walking, swimming)
- Weight loss target: 5-10% body weight (5-10kg) to improve insulin sensitivity
- Alcohol reduction: Target ≤10 standard drinks/week (currently 10-14)
7. Self-monitoring blood glucose (SMBG): Fasting + 2-hour post-prandial readings
REFERRALS AND FOLLOW-UP:
8. Retinal screening: Refer to optometrist/ophthalmologist (overdue - urgent)
9. Dietitian referral: MBS Item 10954 (Chronic Disease Management Plan - up to 5 allied health visits/year)
10. Diabetes educator: Education on SGLT2 inhibitor, SMBG, foot care
MONITORING:
11. Repeat HbA1c in 3 months (target <7%, expect 0.5-1% reduction with SGLT2 inhibitor)
12. Repeat ACR in 6 months (monitor albuminuria trend)
13. Annual influenza vaccination (diabetes = high-risk group)
14. Pneumococcal vaccination if not already given
DIABETES CARE PLAN:
15. Create GP Management Plan (MBS Item 721 + Team Care Arrangement Item 723)
16. Patient education: Hypoglycemia recognition, sick day management, foot care
17. Medical alert bracelet recommendation

critical_errors.error: Failed to escalate therapy despite HbA1c >7% on maximum metformin dose (worsening trend 7.4% → 7.8% → 8.2%)
critical_errors.explanation: PBS criteria for SGLT2 inhibitor met (HbA1c >7% on metformin) - delaying escalation increases cardiovascular/renal complications

critical_errors.error: Stopped ACE inhibitor despite microalbuminuria (ACR 4.2 mg/mmol)
critical_errors.explanation: ACE inhibitor is ESSENTIAL in diabetic nephropathy - stopping accelerates progression to ESKD

critical_errors.error: Failed to claim MBS Item 721 (Diabetes Annual Cycle of Care) despite completing structured review
critical_errors.explanation: Item 721 provides $67.50 rebate for structured diabetes review - financial loss to practice but not clinical error

critical_errors.error: Prescribed SGLT2 inhibitor without checking PBS restrictions (HbA1c >7% on metformin)
critical_errors.explanation: Prescription will be rejected by pharmacist if PBS criteria not documented - causes patient inconvenience

critical_errors.error: Failed to refer for retinal screening despite being 18 months overdue (annual screening required)
critical_errors.explanation: Diabetic retinopathy is leading cause of blindness in working-age adults - delays increase vision loss risk

critical_errors.error: Prescribed sulfonylurea (e.g., gliclazide) as second-line instead of SGLT2 inhibitor despite normal renal function
critical_errors.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors preferred over sulfonylureas (cardiovascular/renal benefits, no hypoglycemia, weight loss vs weight gain)

fracp_reviews.reviewer_credentials: FRACGP (Fellow Royal Australian College of General Practitioners), 22 years post-fellowship, Diabetes educator
fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Excellent - realistic GP presentation with suboptimal control requiring escalation
fracp_reviews.difficulty_appropriate: Yes - Medium difficulty appropriate (chronic disease management, PBS criteria, MBS items)
fracp_reviews.rag_citations_correct: Yes - eTG 3.3 citations verified and accurate
fracp_reviews.feedback: Excellent GP persona. Realistic scenario (truck driver, irregular diet, sedentary). Good emphasis on PBS restrictions for SGLT2 inhibitors (HbA1c >7% on metformin). Consider adding brief mention of cardiovascular risk assessment (Australian Type 2 Diabetes Risk Assessment Tool) for completeness. MBS Item 721 correctly identified.

fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Accurate diabetes management - appropriate escalation pathway (metformin → SGLT2 inhibitor)
fracp_reviews.feedback: Good persona. Management pathway correct (SGLT2 inhibitor preferred over sulfonylurea for CV/renal benefits). Excellent inclusion of microalbuminuria requiring ACE inhibitor continuation. Suggest adding brief mention of GLP-1 agonist as alternative if patient needs greater HbA1c reduction or weight loss (though SGLT2 inhibitor appropriate first choice here).

learning_objectives: Recognize symptoms of suboptimal glycemic control (polyuria, polydipsia, fatigue, worsening HbA1c trend)
Apply Diabetes Annual Cycle of Care framework (HbA1c, lipids, ACR, eGFR, retinal screening, foot exam)
Understand PBS restrictions for SGLT2 inhibitors (HbA1c >7% on metformin monotherapy)
Prescribe SGLT2 inhibitor appropriately (empagliflozin 10mg daily for CV/renal benefits)
Recognize importance of ACE inhibitor in diabetic nephropathy (microalbuminuria detected)
Claim appropriate MBS items (Item 721 Diabetes Annual Cycle of Care, Item 10954 CDM Plan)
Prioritize SGLT2 inhibitor over sulfonylurea as second-line therapy (CV/renal benefits, no hypoglycemia)
Refer for overdue retinal screening (18 months since last screen - annual required)
